niacinamide.title: Niacinamide
niacinamide.lead: A vitamin B3 derivative widely used in cosmetic formulations.
overview: Niacinamide, also known as nicotinamide, is a form of vitamin B3. It is widely used as a cosmetic formulation ingredient.
Its use should be assessed in the context of the complete formulation, intended application, concentration, product format, and applicable regulatory requirements.

considerations.title: Concentration
considerations.text: Select concentration according to the intended product, formulation objectives, technical documentation, and applicable regulatory requirements.

considerations.title: pH
considerations.text: Consider the pH of the complete formulation and the compatibility of niacinamide with the other components.

considerations.title: Stability
considerations.text: Evaluate stability under the actual manufacturing, packaging, storage, and use conditions of the finished product.

hyaluronic-acid.title: Hyaluronic Acid
hyaluronic-acid.lead: A polysaccharide used in cosmetic formulations primarily for its water-binding and film-forming properties.
overview: Hyaluronic acid is a naturally occurring polysaccharide composed of repeating disaccharide units. In cosmetic products, hyaluronic acid and related hyaluronates are used as formulation ingredients with water-binding properties.
Cosmetic performance can vary according to molecular characteristics, concentration, formulation system and processing conditions.

considerations.title: Molecular characteristics
considerations.text: Molecular weight and related material characteristics can influence the sensory and formulation properties of hyaluronic-acid ingredients.

considerations.title: Hydration
considerations.text: Consider the hydration behaviour of the raw material and the complete formulation during processing.

considerations.title: Stability
considerations.text: Evaluate stability in the finished formulation under intended processing, storage and use conditions.

sodium-hyaluronate.title: Sodium Hyaluronate
sodium-hyaluronate.lead: The sodium salt of hyaluronic acid, widely used in cosmetic formulation systems.
overview: Sodium hyaluronate is the sodium salt of hyaluronic acid and is commonly used as a cosmetic formulation ingredient.
Its formulation behaviour depends on material characteristics, concentration, processing conditions and the composition of the finished product.

considerations.title: Material characteristics
considerations.text: Molecular characteristics and raw-material specifications can influence formulation behaviour.

considerations.title: Dispersion
considerations.text: Consider the method used to disperse and hydrate the material during manufacturing.

considerations.title: Finished-product stability
considerations.text: Evaluate stability in the complete formulation under intended storage and use conditions.

panthenol.title: Panthenol
panthenol.lead: A provitamin B5 ingredient used in cosmetic formulations for skin and hair-care applications.
overview: Panthenol is the alcohol analogue of pantothenic acid and is commonly used as a cosmetic formulation ingredient.
Different forms and grades may have different specifications and formulation characteristics.

considerations.title: Grade
considerations.text: Verify the identity, stereochemical form and specification of the raw material supplied for the intended formulation.

considerations.title: Solubility
considerations.text: Consider the material's solubility and incorporation method within the formulation.

considerations.title: Stability
considerations.text: Evaluate stability within the complete formulation and under intended processing and storage conditions.

glycerin.title: Glycerin
glycerin.lead: A polyol widely used in cosmetics and personal-care formulations.
overview: Glycerin, also known as glycerol, is a three-carbon polyol widely used in cosmetic and personal-care formulations.
Its functional contribution depends on concentration and the characteristics of the complete formulation.

considerations.title: Concentration
considerations.text: Consider the concentration required for the intended formulation objective and sensory profile.

considerations.title: Humectancy
considerations.text: Glycerin is commonly incorporated as a humectant and can influence the water-binding behaviour of a formulation.

considerations.title: Sensory properties
considerations.text: Higher concentrations can influence viscosity, tack and overall sensory characteristics.

allantoin.title: Allantoin
allantoin.lead: A heterocyclic compound used as a cosmetic skin-conditioning ingredient.
overview: Allantoin is a naturally occurring compound that is also manufactured synthetically for use in various applications, including cosmetics.
Its use in a formulation should be evaluated according to the intended product and applicable regulatory requirements.

considerations.title: Solubility
considerations.text: Consider the solubility characteristics of allantoin when determining the manufacturing process.

considerations.title: Processing
considerations.text: The order and conditions of addition can influence incorporation into the finished formulation.

considerations.title: Stability
considerations.text: Evaluate the stability of the complete formulation under intended processing and storage conditions.

salicylic-acid.title: Salicylic Acid
salicylic-acid.lead: An aromatic hydroxy acid used in cosmetic and personal-care formulations.
overview: Salicylic acid is an aromatic hydroxy acid used in a range of cosmetic and personal-care formulations.
Its permitted uses and concentration limits can vary by jurisdiction and product category.

considerations.title: Regulatory requirements
considerations.text: Check the regulations applicable to the target market and product category before formulation.

considerations.title: Solubility
considerations.text: Consider the solubility characteristics of salicylic acid and the selected formulation system.

considerations.title: pH
considerations.text: Evaluate the pH of the complete formulation and its relationship to the intended product characteristics.

ascorbic-acid.title: Ascorbic Acid
ascorbic-acid.lead: A water-soluble vitamin and antioxidant used in cosmetic formulations.
overview: Ascorbic acid, commonly known as vitamin C, is a water-soluble vitamin used in cosmetic formulations.
Formulation design can be challenging because chemical stability depends on the formulation environment and processing conditions.

considerations.title: Stability
considerations.text: Evaluate stability carefully under the intended formulation, packaging, storage and use conditions.

considerations.title: pH
considerations.text: The formulation pH can be an important consideration when working with ascorbic acid.

considerations.title: Packaging
considerations.text: Packaging selection should be evaluated alongside the formulation's sensitivity to environmental conditions.

tocopherol.title: Tocopherol
tocopherol.lead: A vitamin E compound used in cosmetic formulations, including as an antioxidant ingredient.
overview: Tocopherol refers to a family of vitamin E compounds. Tocopherol is used as a cosmetic ingredient in a variety of formulation systems.
The properties of a particular raw material depend on its specific identity, composition and supplier specification.

considerations.title: Identity
considerations.text: Verify the specific tocopherol material and supplier specification before formulation.

considerations.title: Oil phase
considerations.text: Consider the formulation phase and incorporation method when using tocopherol.

considerations.title: Oxidative stability
considerations.text: Evaluate the complete formulation and packaging system for stability under intended storage conditions.

caffeine.title: Caffeine
caffeine.lead: A methylxanthine compound used in cosmetic and personal-care formulations.
overview: Caffeine is a methylxanthine compound found naturally in several plant species and used as a cosmetic formulation ingredient.
Its use should be evaluated according to the intended product, formulation system and applicable regulatory requirements.

considerations.title: Solubility
considerations.text: Consider caffeine's solubility and the composition of the formulation when selecting the incorporation method.

considerations.title: Processing
considerations.text: Evaluate the manufacturing process and order of addition to ensure appropriate incorporation.

considerations.title: Stability
considerations.text: Evaluate stability within the complete formulation under intended processing and storage conditions.
